copilot.openingQuestion: Which regulatory items require immediate review?

Which regulatory items require immediate.text: The latest brief carries 17 EMA regulatory documents at the highest urgency (85) and criticality (80) scores. The most recent for review are the PDCO minutes of the 21–24 April 2026 meeting (published 2026-06-03) and the HMA-EMA joint Network Data Steering Group minutes (15 April 2026, published 2026-06-01), alongside the CHMP and CAT meeting agendas. These are official EMA sources with direct document links.

What changed in oncology and advanced th.text: From ASCO26 in the brief: Celcuity was punished as new VIKTORIA-1 data on gedatolisib disappointed investors; in vivo CAR-Ts from Kelonia and Legend drew attention across blood cancers and solid tumours; and AstraZeneca built its case for oral SERD camizestrant with SERENA-6 data. On access, AbbVie's Elahere received an NHS green light for resistant ovarian cancer. On advanced-therapy regulation, the FDA's prior knowledge guide targets cell and gene therapy filings.

Which items are official sources vs news.text: Official regulatory sources in the brief: 17 EMA documents (PDCO, CHMP, CVMP, CAT, COMP, PRAC, Management Board and shortage-related steering group agendas and minutes). News sources: 8 items from endpoints, including the FDA prior knowledge guide, the Elahere NHS green light, Lilly's Ascidian alliance, NewLimit's financing, and three ASCO26 items. Official EMA items carry the highest confidence given direct document links.

Summarize today's highest-criticality si.text: Highest-criticality signals are the EMA regulatory documents (urgency 85, criticality 80): the PDCO minutes of the 21–24 April 2026 meeting and the HMA-EMA joint Network Data Steering Group minutes, plus the CHMP and CAT meeting agendas. Lower-criticality but strategically relevant news (urgency 45) includes Lilly's $1.9bn Ascidian alliance and AbbVie's Elahere NHS green light.
